title: UK Construction Output Growth, May 2026
question: What will the first ONS estimate of total construction output in Great Britain, seasonally adjusted chained volume measure, month-on-month percentage growth be for May 2026?
resolutionSource: Office for National Statistics Construction output in Great Britain: May 2026 and Output in the construction industry: all-work summary
resolutionRule: Resolve to the first ONS-published estimate for May 2026 monthly total construction output in Great Britain, seasonally adjusted chained volume measure, all work, month-on-month percentage growth, rounded to one decimal place. Use the value in the first Construction output in Great Britain: May 2026 release or its associated Output in the construction industry all-work summary dataset on 16 July 2026; ignore later revisions.
drivers: April growth slowed to 0.1% after March's 1.5% financial-year push
three-month total output momentum was positive at 1.6% to April 2026
repair and maintenance was stronger than new work in April
Q1 2026 new orders fell 10.5%, limiting upside for new work
recent monthly volatility implies about 0.75 percentage-point sigma

reasoning.text: UK construction output growth, May 2026 first print

Framing and exact resolver: target is ONS total construction output in Great Britain, all work, chained volume measure, seasonally adjusted, month-on-month percent growth for May 2026. I use the same SA all-work monthly growth variant for all anchors; the all-work summary dataset page is the table source, while the May 2026 bulletin is the first-print resolution page.

reasoning.call: ONS latest construction output bulletin and all-work summary dataset schedule lookup
reasoning.result: The latest ONS construction output bulletin was for April 2026, released 12 June 2026, and both the bulletin and all-work summary dataset state the next release is 16 July 2026.

reasoning.call: ONS April 2026 construction output bulletin main-points lookup
reasoning.result: Fetched latest same-variant values: monthly total construction output grew 0.1% in April 2026, after 1.5% in March 2026 and 0.5% in February 2026; three-month total output grew 1.6% to April 2026.

reasoning.call: ONS March 2026 construction output bulletin lookup for components and orders
reasoning.result: Fetched March 2026 details: monthly total output grew 1.5%, new work grew 2.0%, repair and maintenance grew 0.8%, and Q1 2026 new orders fell 10.5% versus Q4 2025.

reasoning.call: ONS previous releases lookup for recent monthly reference class
reasoning.result: Fetched same-variant recent monthly growth prints, using latest revised values available before the May 2026 first print where available: July 2025 0.2%, August 2025 -0.3%, September 2025 0.2%, October 2025 -0.6%, November 2025 -1.3%, December 2025 -0.5%, January 2026 0.2%, February 2026 0.5%, March 2026 1.5%, April 2026 0.1%.

reasoning.text: Base rate/reference class: the recent official-source monthly all-work SA growth reference class is centered near flat, with mean 0.00% over the ten fetched monthly observations. I anchor near that base rate rather than extrapolating March's 1.5% because ONS described March as helped by financial year-end pushes and April already slowed to 0.1%.

Current-release update: level and momentum are mildly positive because the three-month measure rose 1.6% and April did not reverse March's jump. One-off effect is negative because the March financial-year push should not repeat in May. Policy/mechanism pressure is slightly negative from Q1 new orders down 10.5%, but construction output can lag orders, so I do not make a large near-term cut.

Prior/update/interval: persistence/base-rate prior uses the ten ONS same-variant monthly growth values from July 2025 through April 2026, using latest revised values available before the May 2026 first print where available: 0.2, -0.3, 0.2, -0.6, -1.3, -0.5, 0.2, 0.5, 1.5, 0.1. Mean = 0.00. sigma = 0.75 using sample standard deviation of those values themselves because this is already a change/flow series. 80% half-width = 1.28*sigma = 0.96. Point update: 0.00 base rate + 0.15 positive three-month momentum - 0.05 March one-off/new-orders drag = 0.10. Rounded 80% interval: 0.10 +/- 0.96 gives about -0.9 to 1.1.

Counter-consideration: upside risk is a continued repair-and-maintenance surge plus resilient new-work site activity, which would land above the interval if May prints above 1.1%. Downside risk is delayed new work, weak private new housing, or order-book pass-through from lower new orders, which would land outside the interval below -0.9%.
